failures.criterion: Delivered item 1 of dispatch://INFRA-623/spec: 'a jj command that creates a repository refuses to run under an enclosing .jj'. It does not refuse, and provisioning writes that repository exactly as before the fix, when the state directory is reached through a symlink — the configuration config.go:352-353 states is allowed ('The state directory itself is not checked: an operator may reach it through a symlink'), standing on the live operator case the fix exists for (a legion.yaml kept inside a checkout). refuseEnclosingWorkspace (config.go:404) walks the lexical path with filepath.Dir, so a symlink component hides the enclosing .jj, while the child chdir'd there asks the kernel where it stands and jj walks up from the resolved path and opens that repository.
failures.evidence: Red test: packages/daemon/internal/workspace/enclosingsymlink_test.go, TestAStateDirectoryReachedThroughASymlinkIsRefusedInsideARepository, committed at b932555c3cdf. `go -C packages/daemon test -count=1 -run 'TestAStateDirectoryReachedThroughASymlinkIsRefusedInsideARepository' ./internal/workspace` fails at the head (3e2c3045): 'Provision through the symlink .../state-link made .../state-link/repos/github.com/acme/widgets, want a refusal'. Measured first on the production CLI, not in a test: a decoy colocated jj repository with the legacy .jj/repo/config.toml, a `state` directory inside it and a symlink to that directory from outside; `legion workspace-init provision --issue INFRA-623 --repo sjawhar/legion --default-branch main --root <the symlink> --credential-helper '!legion git-credential' --feed /legion/feed`, built at the head, exits 0 reporting success and writes config-id into the decoy's .jj/repo (jj-content digest 8702b51b055905c6 before, 45631683d08a5cd1 after). The same command with --root a real path inside the decoy is refused, exit 1, so only the symlink gets past the guard. The test is satisfiable: in a scratch copy of the head, resolving the longest existing prefix of the directory before the walk (filepath.EvalSymlinks on each ancestor that exists, rejoining the rest, so a directory that is not there yet still resolves) makes it pass with TestProvisionLeavesTheEnclosingRepositoryUntouched, TestAJJThatCreatesARepositoryIsRefusedInsideOne, TestTheRunnerRefusesACommandWithNoAbsoluteWorkingDirectory and TestJJWorkspaceRootIsTheRepositoryFlagAlone all green (ok 12.943s); a bare filepath.EvalSymlinks(dir) does not, since it refuses the two 'a directory that is not there yet' cases of the implementer's own unit test.

proof.surface: The same `legion workspace-init provision` run from $LEGION_WORKSPACE, with PATH shims for git and jj that log each child's own `pwd -P`, its argv and its GIT_CONFIG_* environment before exec'ing the real binary, so the instrument reads the production execRunner's children rather than a test double.
